marketplace.summary: Capell pages arrive in your Vue app as ready-made Vue 3 components, and Vue is the default, so no setting needs changing.
marketplace.description: Vue 3 components for Capell pages, for teams who write their public site in Vue. Vue is the default adapter, so installing this package is enough to select it. The npm packages your build needs are declared for you.
marketplace.problem: Our developers write Vue, and I don't want them building a client for Capell pages from nothing.
marketplace.outcome: Your Vue developers start from working page and widget components while editors stay in the Capell admin.

faq.question: Do I need to change a setting to use the Vue adapter?
faq.answer: No. Vue is the adapter Capell Inertia uses until told otherwise, so choosing it needs no setting, only installing it.

faq.question: What does it add to my front-end build?
faq.answer: Vue 3.5, Inertia's Vue library and Vite's Vue integration. The adapter declares all three for you.

faq.question: Does it come with a look of its own?
faq.answer: No. The components carry class names such as capell-inertia-page but no styles, so your stylesheet decides the look.

faq.question: What shows for a widget that has no Vue component of its own?
faq.answer: Content, image and title widgets have components of their own. Any other type is drawn by the content component, which shows only its title and content.
